descriptionChirho: Aramaic noun denoting nobles, grandees, or lords of the royal court; an intensified reduplicative form from rab 'great,' designating high-ranking officials in the Babylonian/Persian imperial hierarchy. All three clusters are inflectional variants with different pronominal suffixes: 3ms 'his nobles' (eng: and his nobles / his nobles, spa: y sus nobles / sus nobles, arb: وَ عُظَمَاؤُهُ / وَ عُظَمَائِهِ, kor: 그리고 그의 귀족들, swa: na wakuu wake / wakuu wake), 2ms 'your nobles' as ketiv/qere (eng: and your nobles, spa: y tus nobles, hin: और तेरे प्रधान, arb: وَ عُظَمَاؤُكَ, swa: na wakuu wako), and 1cs 'my nobles' (eng: and my nobles, spa: y mis nobles, hin: और मेरे प्रधान, arb: وَ عُظَمَائِي, swa: na wakuu wangu). Attested exclusively in Daniel 4-6 (Dan 4:33; 5:1,2,3,9,10,23; 6:18).
